decisions.quote: To replicate the estimates of the effect of the bank branch expansion on rural poverty outcomes, we used the same dataset5 as Burgess and Pande (2005). The dataset is from the Reserve Bank of India. It contains the information on bank branch opening dates, locations, and state characteristics (poverty, wages, expenditure, land reform, and population) from 1961 to 2000 in 16 Indian states.
decisions.reason: The study re-analyses the exact same 1961-2000 dataset and Stata code from Burgess and Pande (2005) downloaded from the AEA website, without collecting new data or using a new sample. Under the codebook, re-analysing the original study's own data and code is a reproduction.

decisions.quote: We successfully reiterate their empirical results; however, we find significant trend reversals for almost every other year between 1970 and 1984. These results, along with the historical evidence on policy changes in India, imply that Burgess and Pande (2005) overestimate the effect of the bank branch expansion on poverty. Unlike Kochar (2011), we obtain these results with the same data as used by Burgess and Pande (2005) in the original paper.1
decisions.location: Section 1 Introduction, p. 3 (see also Section 3.3.2, p. 14 and Section 5 Conclusion, pp. 19-21)
decisions.reason: Because the study is a reproduction, outcome is coded on the two reproduction axes. In Section 3, the authors exactly reproduce the original reduced-form and IV estimates of Burgess and Pande (2005) ('the results are precisely the same as in Burgess and Pande (2005)'), establishing 'computationally reproducible' for outcome_computation. In Section 4, repeating the analysis across alternative cut-years (1970-1984) reveals significant trend reversals across almost all cut-years (maximized in 1980 when the IRDP was implemented), leading the authors to conclude that the 1977 instrument is not uniquely exogenous, does not prove a superior impact of bank branch expansion, and overestimates the effects of bank expansion on poverty reduction, establishing 'robustness challenges' for outcome_robustness.
